main_text.head: PROBLEMA I.

head.i: An ars liberalis recte distribuatur in contemplatricem & operatricem?

main_text.p: Thesis affirm.ARistoteles passim in suis libris, praesertim lib. 6. Me-taph. c. 1. tria genera scientiarum, hoc est, discipli-defend.narum & artium constituit. Unum vocat θεωρητικὸν[?], contemplativum: Alterum πρακτικὸν[?], actiuum: Tertium, ποιητικὸν[?], effectiuum. Ratio illius distributionis sumitur partim a subiecto doctrinali, partim a fine disciplinarum. Alia enim versatur περὶ τὰ θεωρητὰ[?], hoc est, res solummodo contemplandas: alia, περὶ τὰ πρακτὰ[?], hoc est, res agendas; alia περὶ τὰ ποιητὰ[?], hoc est, circa res efficiendas: & rursus alia solam cognitionem rerum circa quas versatur sibi habet propositam; alia praeter cognitionem, etiam actionem; alia effectionem. Sed Zabar. lib. 1. de nat. Log. c. 2. & alibi trimembrem illam distributionem Aristotelis, ad bimembrem revocat. Itaque disciplinam aliam dicit esse contemplatricem, aliam operatricem. Et hanc rur-sus vel πρακτικὴν[?] vel ποιητικὴν[?].

Obiectio.Caeterum hanc distributionem multis seculis in scho-lis approbatam, quidam recentiores Philosophi in du-I.bium vocant; & his argumentis impugnant. 1, Quia membra distributionis inter se non dissentiunt. Nulla enim ars est, quae in sola rerum, quas tractat, cognitione acquiescat, neque eam ad certum aliquem vitae humanae usum transferat. Ideoque quaelibet ars simul est contemplatrix & operatrix.

page.notes: Printed page number read as "19"; the glyph is slightly worn. Greek words with accents and breathings were read with uncertainty and are marked [?]; the Greek compound in item 46 is especially doubtful. The word "nullū" has a probable macron over the u, marked [?]. The initial "A" of the first paragraph is a large initial, joined to "Ristoteles". The paragraph beginning "2, Quia" carries on to the next page after "ha-". The line "Quia membra" is printed "Qu'a" with an apparent apostrophe, read as Quia.
